name: Euodia
overview: Euodia is a female believer mentioned in the New Testament, specifically in the book of Philippians. She is noted for being urged by the Apostle Paul to live in harmony within the Lord, highlighting her role in the early Christian community. Beyond this, Scripture does not provide further personal details or tribal affiliation.
namesAndTitles: The name Euodia appears once in Scripture and is presented without a specific meaning or divine origin. It is simply recorded as her proper name in Philippians 4:2.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Euodia beyond her mention in the context of Christian fellowship and unity as urged by Paul.
scriptureSignificance: Euodia holds significance in the biblical narrative as an example of a believer whose unity with others was important to the health of the early church. Paul's direct appeal for her to live in harmony underscores the value placed on peace and cooperation among believers. Her mention reflects the practical challenges and spiritual exhortations present in the New Testament church.
